memory_candidates.content: A script contracted to emit exactly one JSON line on stdout (a 'decision line' consumed by a caller via command substitution) must redirect the stdout of every shared helper it calls, not just its own echoes. Several common lifecycle helpers in this codebase print their own diagnostic text to real stdout with no redirect of their own: git-commit-scoped.sh's final `echo "$commit_output"`, update-task-status.sh's `OK: task N status -> ...` line (reached transitively through skill_postflight_update), and generate-todo.sh's own output (reached transitively through skill_link_artifacts). Calling any of these from inside a single-JSON-line-contract script without appending `>&2` at the CALL SITE silently corrupts the caller's own stdout contract -- caught only by an integration test that actually parses the script's stdout as JSON (a stub-based unit test of the same call site would not have caught it, since a stub does not reproduce the leaked stdout). The fix is always at the call site (redirect), never inside the shared helper (which has its own legitimate callers that want that stdout visible).

The bash parameter-expansion landmine `"${var:-{}}"` (intending 'default to empty-object JSON') is NOT just a documented pitfall in one place in this codebase (skill_orchestrate_propagate_completion's own header comment in skill-base.sh) -- it is easy to independently reintroduce, because it looks correct and even mostly works: bash's default-word matching stops at the FIRST unescaped `}`, so a NON-empty $var gets a stray trailing `}` appended, producing invalid JSON. A `jq -r '.field // "default"' 2>/dev/null` read against that corrupted JSON often still prints the CORRECT value to stdout before jq hits the trailing garbage and exits nonzero on a parse error -- so a naive `$(...) || fallback="..."` idiom silently discards the correct value and substitutes the fallback, with no visible error (stderr was suppressed). The only safe pattern is `var="$x"; [ -z "$var" ] && var='{}'` (a plain -z test, never inline default-word `:-`) before ever piping the variable into jq. Grep for `:-{}}"` when reviewing any new script that defaults a possibly-empty JSON variable this way.
